The ONE approved exception: on cinder-rs2-arwc you may call the connector's earn_corporate once to seed the corporate session, as the stand-in for the KeplerOps pivot (the real pivot is proven separately). Every other state must come from doing the cards as a participant. Commands are monitored automatically for state writes.

FIX MODE (when a documented step fails): diagnose with operator access on your range only (logs, inspect, reading source). Fix the CODE, SEED, or CONFIG in the code tree /tmp/cinder-dev-release/cinder-typhoon/ (the only complete code tree; edit real files minimally; do not commit). Apply the change to your range by rebuilding or recreating the service, then produce all state as a participant. Prefer the native implementation (ERPNext, Nextcloud, Keycloak, OT layer); never restart retired facade containers (a-hmi, a-historian, a-reservoir, a-distribution). If the fix needs a design decision or another range, post type blocker and move on. 20 minutes max per fix.

RULE (from the user): no card may depend on a credential, token, or session that expires and then blocks the participant until an operator resets something. Acceptable: (a) it stays valid for the life of the range (ranges may be provisioned days before the event), or (b) the participant can obtain a fresh one through the card path, or (c) the service renews it itself. If you find any expiring credential that strands a participant, treat it as a failing card and fix the root cause in the code tree (seed duration, service self-renewal, or a participant re-issue path), then post the fix.

ADDENDUM (from the user): participants must always be able to retrace their steps to get themselves going again. Beyond expiring credentials, this covers single-use steps: if a step can only be done once (a one-time redeem, a consumed token, a state change that cannot be repeated), a participant who loses the result must be able to recover it by retracing the documented path (for example the repeated request returns the same session or result for the same input, or there is a documented re-issue route), without an operator reset. Check every card in your scope, including cards already passed, and fix any dead end in the code tree. Known example: Training T02.3 /api/recovery/redeem returns 409 on a second redeem, which strands a participant who lost the session token.
